inline.s: Bodhisattva Maitreya said to the Buddha: “World-Honored One, as the Buddha has spoken, each one of them is seen.” Maitreya then said: “Why is it that in this world a certain class of beings, though they too cultivate goodness, do not seek rebirth there?”
The Buddha told Maitreya: “The wisdom of such beings is shallow and slight. Discriminating the Western land as inferior to the heavens, they take no delight in it and do not seek rebirth there.”
Maitreya said: “These beings, with false discrimination, do not seek the Buddha-land. How shall they escape the round of birth and death?”
The Buddha said to Maitreya: “In the Land of Ultimate Bliss, is there birth from the womb?”

Maitreya said: “No, World-Honored One. Those born there are like the devas of the desire realm, dwelling in palaces five hundred yojanas wide and sporting there in freedom. How could there be birth from the womb? World-Honored One, by what cause and what condition are the beings of this world born from the womb?”

The Buddha said to Maitreya: “These beings plant roots of goodness, yet cannot transcend appearances. They do not seek the Buddha's wisdom, but give rise to false discrimination. Deeply attached to worldly pleasures and to blessings among humans, they are therefore born from the womb. But if there are beings who, with the wisdom of no appearances, plant the roots of every virtue, whose body and mind are pure and who are far removed from discrimination, who seek birth in the pure land and tend toward the Buddha's bodhi — such a person, at the end of life, in a single instant, is seated upon a jeweled lotus in the Buddha's Pure Land, complete in bodily form. How could there be birth from the womb? Maitreya, you see the foolish and deluded, who plant no roots of goodness but rely on worldly wisdom and clever argument, give rise to false discrimination and increase their crooked minds — how shall they escape the great calamity of birth and death? There are also beings who, though they plant roots of goodness, make offering to the Three Jewels, and create a great field of blessing, yet grasp at appearances, discriminate, and cling with deep emotion. Though they seek to escape the round of rebirth, in the end they cannot attain it. The Buddha told Maitreya: suppose a king of the kṣatriya caste, established in the rank of consecration, were to build a great prison, and within that prison set halls, towers, and pavilions, railings and windows, couches and seats, all adorned with precious jewels; and whatever clothing, food, or drink he might need were all provided in abundance. Then the consecrated king drives out the crown prince and shuts him fast within the prison. He further gives him money, wealth, and precious treasures, fine silks and bolts of cloth, to enjoy as he pleases. The Buddha told Maitreya: what do you think? Would that prince obtain happiness?”

Maitreya said: “No, World-Honored One. Though within it there are halls, towers, and pavilions, food and clothing, money and silk, gold and jewels to enjoy as he pleases, yet his body is locked in prison and his mind is not at ease. He seeks only to get out.”
The Buddha told Maitreya: “If the consecrated king does not renounce his fault, could his ministers, elders, and householders cause the prince to be freed from the prison?”
Maitreya said: “Since the king does not renounce it, how could he get out?”

The Buddha said: “So it is, so it is. Those beings, though they cultivate blessings and make offering to the Three Jewels, yet with false discrimination seek the fruits of humans and devas. When the reward comes, the world they dwell in, the palaces and pavilions, the clothing and bedding, the food and drink and medicine — all that they need is fully abundant. Yet they cannot get out of the prison of the three realms; they forever dwell in the round of rebirth, without freedom. Even if father and mother, wife and children, sons and daughters, and kin wished to save and deliver them, in the end they could not escape, for the king of wrong views cannot be renounced and left behind. But if beings cut off false discrimination, plant the roots of every goodness, and are without appearances and without clinging, they shall be born in the Buddha-land and attain liberation forever.”

The Buddha said to Maitreya: “In this Sahā world of mine there are seventy-two koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who have already made offering to immeasurable Buddhas, planted the roots of every virtue, and shall be born in that land, draw near to make offering to the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, and accomplish anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.

Again, Ānanda, in the Buddha-land of Patience-Enduring there are eighteen koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who shall be born in that land. In the Buddha-land of Precious Treasury there are ninety koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who shall be born in that land. In the Buddha-land of Fire Light there are twenty-two koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who shall be born in that land. In the Buddha-land of Immeasurable Light there are twenty-five koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who shall be born in that land. In the Buddha-land of World Lamp there are sixty koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who shall be born in that land. In the Buddha-land of Dragon Tree there are one thousand four hundred bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who shall be born in that land. In the Buddha-land of Stainless Light there are twenty-five koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who shall be born in that land. In the Buddha-land of the Lion there are one thousand eight hundred bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who shall be born in that land. In the Buddha-land of Auspicious Peak there are two thousand one hundred koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who shall be born in that land. In the Buddha-land of the Humane King there are one thousand koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who shall be born in that land. In the Buddha-land of Flower Banner there is one koṭi of bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who shall be born in that land. In the Buddha-land of Light King there are twelve koṭis of bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who shall be born in that land. In the Buddha-land of Fearlessness Attained there are sixty-nine koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattvas mahāsattvas who shall be born in that land; all of them shall draw near to make offering to the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, and before long shall accomplish anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.

The Buddha said to Maitreya: “Such are the majestic virtues of the Land of Ultimate Bliss. Were I to speak of them for measureless kalpas beyond all reckoning, I could not come to the end of them. If a good man or good woman hears the name of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, gives rise to a single thought of faith, and takes refuge, reveres, and venerates him, you should know that such a person is no follower of the lesser vehicle: in my Dharma he is named the foremost disciple.”

The Buddha told Maitreya: “If monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, together with devas, dragons, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, and humans and non-humans, write out and make offering to this sutra, receive, uphold, read, and recite it, expound it for others, and even for a single day and night contemplate that land and the merit of the Buddha's body, such a person at the end of life shall swiftly attain birth there and accomplish anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi.”

Again, Maitreya, this sutra is most profound and subtle, and brings wide benefit to beings. If there are beings who receive, uphold, read, and recite this true Dharma, write it out, and make offering to it, then though at that person's death the three-thousand great thousandfold world be filled with a great fire, he can still pass beyond it and be born in that land. Such a person has already met the Buddhas of the past and received from them the prediction of bodhi; all the Tathāgatas praise him with one voice, and supreme bodhi is accomplished for him as he wishes. The Buddha said to Maitreya: “A Buddha's appearance in the world is hard to meet, and the true Dharma is hard to hear; what the Tathāgata has practiced, you should likewise practice. Guard this sutra greatly, for the long night's benefit of sentient beings. Do not let beings fall into the five paths, into splendor-adorned hells; rather cause all sentient beings to plant and cultivate goodness and blessing, and seek birth in the pure land. Then the World-Honored One spoke in verse:
Unless in former lives one cultivated merit and wisdom, one cannot hear this true Dharma.
But those who once made offering to the Tathāgatas — it is they who hear this meaning now.
And having heard it, hold, recite, and write it out, to read and praise and make offering too.
Whoever seeks the Pure Land with single mind shall surely be reborn in the Land of Bliss.
And should a great fire fill the three thousand vast, and all the prisons that with splendor shine,
all such distress he can pass safely by, through the Tathāgata's majestic power.
The benefits and virtues of that Buddha — the Buddha alone with a Buddha can know.
Should the whole world be filled with hearers and with pratyekabuddhas through all space,
exhausting all their spiritual powers, they still could not fathom it at all.
Should there be beings of long life whose years abide for koṭis of kalpas without end,
praising the Tathāgata's body of merit, to the end of life their praise would not be spent.
The Dharma that the great Sage, the Dharma King, proclaimed brings benefit to every living being.
Whoever receives and holds it in reverence — the Buddha calls that one a true good friend.

Then, when the World-Honored One spoke this Dharma, there were twelve koṭis of nayutas of people who, far from dust and defilement, obtained the pure Dharma eye. Eight hundred monks, their outflows exhausted and their minds understood, attained liberation of mind. Among the assembly of devas and humans, there were twenty-two koṭis of nayutas of people who realized the fruit of the non-returner. There were again twenty-five koṭis of people who attained the patient acceptance of the Dharma without retreat. There were again forty koṭis, a hundred thousand nayutas of people, who aroused the mind of anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi, planted all roots of goodness, and all vowed to be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss and to see the Buddha of Immeasurable Life. And from Buddha-lands in the ten directions, those who in the present are born, and those who in the future shall be born, and who see the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, were each of them eight myriads of koṭis of nayutas of people. They received from Dīpaṃkara Buddha the prediction, with the name Wondrous Sound Tathāgata, and shall attain anuttarā-samyak-saṃbodhi. All those beings, through the causal conditions of the former vows of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, were together born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.

When the Buddha spoke these words, the three-thousand great thousandfold world quaked in six ways, and fragrant flowers rained down, piling up to the knee. There were also devas who, in the empty sky, made wondrous music and uttered sounds of rejoicing. And even the devas of the form realm all heard it, and sighed in praise of what had never been.

Then the venerable Ānanda, together with Bodhisattva Maitreya and the rest, and the devas, dragons, and the eight kinds of beings, the whole great assembly, hearing what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly joyful, and received it with faith, and honored and practiced it.
